}

Count inner iterations first, then multiply by outer iterations.

    System.out.print(i + " ");
    i++;
}

Common Mistake
Watch Out!

Changing the loop type without fixing the condition doesn't guarantee correctness.

AP Exam Strategy

For "inclusive" loops, check whether your condition should use `<` or `<=`.

Advanced Practice Question

Format: Boolean Precedence (&& with ||)

What is printed? 
int a = 4;
int b = 5;

boolean r = (a < b) && (a + b == 9) || (a == 0);

System.out.println(r);
Difficulty: Hard  |  Topic: Boolean Precedence (&& with ||)  |  Cycle: 2 (Advanced)
Why This Answer?

`a < b` is true and `a + b == 9` is true, so `(true && true)` is true. `a == 0` is false. `true || false` is true.

Common Mistake
Watch Out!

Forgetting that `&&` is evaluated before `||` unless parentheses change it.

AP Exam Strategy

If you're unsure, rewrite as: `((a < b) && (a + b == 9)) || (a == 0)`.

Advanced Practice Question

Format: Boolean Precedence (&& before ||)

What is printed? 
int a = 3;
int b = 7;

boolean result = (a > 3) || (b / a == 2) && (b % a == 1);

System.out.println(result);
Difficulty: Hard  |  Topic: Boolean Precedence (&& before ||)  |  Cycle: 2 (Advanced)
Why This Answer?

`a > 3` is false. `b / a` is `7 / 3` which is 2 (integer division), so `(b / a == 2)` is true. `b % a` is 1, so `(b % a == 1)` is true. `true && true` is true, so `false || true` is true.

Common Mistake
Watch Out!

Evaluating left-to-right and treating `||` as having the same precedence as `&&`.

AP Exam Strategy

Remember: `&&` groups tighter than `||` unless parentheses force a different grouping.

int count = 0;

for (int i = 0; i < 10; i += 3)
{
    count++;
}

System.out.println(count);
Difficulty: Hard  |  Topic: Iteration (for-loop count)  |  Cycle: 2 (Advanced)
Why This Answer?

`i` takes values 0, 3, 6, 9 (four iterations). Each iteration increments `count`, so it prints 4.

Common Mistake
Watch Out!

Stopping at `i = 6` and forgetting `i = 9` still satisfies `i < 10`.

AP Exam Strategy

List the actual `i` values the loop uses; don't guess.

Format: Iteration (while-loop tracing)

What is printed? 
int x = 20;
int y = 0;

while (x > 0)
{
    x -= 6;
    y++;
}

System.out.println(y);
Difficulty: Hard  |  Topic: Iteration (while-loop tracing)  |  Cycle: 2 (Advanced)
Why This Answer?

x goes 20 → 14 → 8 → 2 → -4. The loop ran 4 times, so y is 4.

Common Mistake
Watch Out!

Assuming the loop stops when x becomes 2 (it stops only after the next subtraction makes x ≤ 0).

AP Exam Strategy

Track x after each update; the condition is checked at the top each time.
